ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper left of the figure gives M(ω), whose spectrum is drawn on the frequency axis; the upper right gives the filter H1(ω), which presents a triangular amplitude-frequency response, centered at ω=0, and marks a finite nonzero frequency range. The lower block diagram shows that the signal m(t) first passes through H1(ω) to obtain m'(t), and then is multiplied by the impulse sampling sequence to obtain the sampled signal. Reasoning: What the problem asks is the sampling rate when the output signal after filtering by H1(ω) is ideally sampled. According to the given method, from H1(ω) in the figure, take its limiting range for the relevant spectrum as |ω| ≤ 10ω1, therefore the highest angular frequency of the sampled signal is B = 10ω1. According to the Nyquist sampling criterion in angular-frequency form, the sampling angular frequency must satisfy ωs ≥ 2B, so ωs ≥ 2 × 10ω1 = 20ω1.

raw_record.question_text: The frequency spectrum \( M(\omega) \) of a signal \( m(t) \) is shown in (a). After passing through a filter with transfer function \( H_1(\omega) \) shown below, it is then ideally sampled. What should the sampling rate be?

method.method_draft: Identify the signal being sampled as the output after the H1(ω) filter. From the diagram, take H1(ω) to limit the relevant spectrum to |ω| ≤ 10ω1. Therefore the highest angular frequency present is B = 10ω1. Apply the Nyquist criterion ωs ≥ 2B, giving ωs ≥ 20ω1.
